# ADR-111 Rule Set ↔ FedRAMP CR26 KSI Catalog — Reconciliation

**Date Code:** 2026-07-09 10:48 ET
**Status:** Draft (UIAO-side; not part of the OrgComp corpus)
**Resolves:** OrgComp evidence-layer open item #1 ("KSI-count reconciliation")
**Authorities:** UIAO_207 (Current), UIAO_137 (Draft v0.2), ADR-126, ADR-061, official FedRAMP CR26 JSON `2026.06.24.01`

---

## 0. The headline

The OrgComp roadmap lists "diff the 29-rule set against the CR26 Moderate catalog" as
its #1 open item and guesses the catalog holds "~56–63 indicators." **Most of that
diff already exists in UIAO canon, and the guess is wrong.** Reconciling the two
document sets surfaces a live three-way number conflict that materially qualifies
OrgComp's "29/29 satisfied" claim.

![The KSI-count reconciliation: three numbers that do not yet agree — AAN's 29 rules, UIAO canon's 14 local rules, and the official CR26 catalog's 46 indicators — over a coverage bar showing 21 indicators covered (about 46 percent), 10 partial-theme gaps, and 15 zero-coverage indicators across five whole themes (CED, INR, PIY, RPL, SCR). Blueprint diagram, OrgComp house style.](figs/uiao-diagram-03-cr26-reconciliation.png)

---

## 1. The three-way number conflict

| Source | Says | Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| OrgComp roadmap + Book 00 | "29 KSI rules (ADR-111); **29/29 satisfied**"; catalog "~56–63 indicators" | 2026-07-07 | Draft (inbox, not canon) |
| UIAO_137 (KSI mapping spec) | "**14 local KSI rules** (KSI-001…014); cover **21 of 46** CR26 indicators (~46%)" | 2026-06-18 | Draft canon |
| UIAO_207 (CR26 assessment) | Official CR26 = "**10 themes / 46 KSI indicators**"; verified vs official JSON | 2026-07-01 | **Current canon** |

Three things fall out immediately:

1. **The catalog size is settled: 46 KSI indicators**, not 56–63. UIAO_207 vendored
   the *official* FedRAMP JSON (`2026.06.24.01`, SHA pinned) and confirmed all 46
   indicator IDs and theme assignments. OrgComp's "~56–63" guess can be retired.
2. **The rule count conflicts: 29 (OrgComp) vs 14 (UIAO canon).** As of 2026-07-01,
   Current canon (UIAO_207 §7) recognizes **14** local KSI rules in
   `src/uiao/ksi/rules/` (KSI-001…014). OrgComp's KSI-015…029 do not appear in the
   canonical rule corpus. Either they are OrgComp-side scaffolds never landed as rule
   files, or a parallel numbering. **This must be reconciled first** — the count
   the AR asserts has to match the rule files that exist.
3. **"29/29 satisfied" ≠ full CR26 coverage.** Even taken at face value, "29 rules
   pass" is a statement about an internal rule set. Canonical coverage of the
   *indicator surface* is **21 of 46 (~46%)**, with **15 indicators (5 whole
   themes) at zero coverage**.

---

## 2. What UIAO canon has already resolved

The reconciliation the OrgComp roadmap defers is largely done:

- **Authority pinned** — official CR26 JSON vendored under ADR-126 (SHA
  `48d1fb4c…`), superseding the earlier Palladium OSCAL snapshot as the rules-text
  authority. The two agree on all 46 indicator IDs.
- **Forward map done** — UIAO_137 §3 maps each of the 14 local rules to its CR26
  theme-prefixed indicator IDs, with per-row confidence (high/medium) and rationale.
- **Reverse map done** — UIAO_137 §4 lists, per CR26 theme, which indicators have a
  local rule and which are gaps.
- **FRR surface assessed** — UIAO_207 §5 rates all 17 FRR categories (9 Covered,
  5 Partial, 3 External) with 8 named gap items.
- **Drift-gated** — the `fedramp-cr26-catalog` adapter emits `DRIFT-PROVENANCE` if
  any cited CR26 ID stops resolving in the pinned snapshot, so the map cannot
  silently rot.

So the UIAO-side answer to open item #1 is not "to be done" — it is "done to ~46%
indicator coverage, with the residual explicitly enumerated." OrgComp's roadmap simply
does not reflect it (correctly — OrgComp is kept UIAO-free).

---

## 3. The reconciled coverage table (CR26 KSI, all 46)

Per UIAO_137 §4. "Covered" = at least one local KSI rule contributes evidence.

| CR26 theme | Indicators | Local-rule coverage | Gap |
|---|---:|---|---|
| KSI-IAM Identity & Access | 6 | **6/6** (KSI-001…009) | — |
| KSI-CMT Change Management | 4 | 4/4 **scaffold** (KSI-011…014, not yet evaluable) | evidence binding pending CR26 VER |
| KSI-SVC Service Config | 8 | 4/8 (KSI-004/006/007/008/010) | 4 indicators |
| KSI-CNA Cloud Native Arch | 8 | 2/8 (KSI-007/008) | 6 indicators |
| KSI-MLA Monitoring/Logging | 5 | 2/5 (KSI-005) | 3 indicators |
| KSI-CED Cybersecurity Edu | 1 | **0/1** | RAT |
| KSI-INR Incident Response | 3 | **0/3** | AAR·RIR·RPI |
| KSI-PIY Policy & Inventory | 5 | **0/5** | GIV·RES·RIS·RSD·RVD |
| KSI-RPL Recovery Planning | 4 | **0/4** | ABO·ARP·RRO·TRC |
| KSI-SCR Supply Chain | 2 | **0/2** | MIT·MON |
| **Total** | **46** | **21 covered (~46%)** | **25 residual; 15 in 5 zero-coverage themes** |

**The paradox to resolve:** OrgComp says these themes are *closed* (Book 14 closes
CP/RPL; Book 06 closes IR/INR; Book 04 closes PT/PIY; Book 05 closes AT/CED; Book 02
closes SR/SCR). The controls *are* architecturally closed. But there is **no local
KSI rule** turning that closure into a continuously-evaluable indicator. OrgComp counts
the closure; UIAO_137 counts the evaluator. Both are right about different things —
which is exactly why the claim language must be precise.

---

## 4. Corrected claim language

| Instead of (OrgComp roadmap) | Say |
|---|---|
| "the CR26 Moderate catalog (~56–63 indicators)" | "the CR26 catalog: **46 KSI indicators** across 10 themes (official JSON `2026.06.24.01`)" |
| "29/29 KSI rules satisfied" | "the internal rule set passes; **CR26 indicator coverage is 21/46 (~46%)** with 15 indicators across 5 themes not yet wired to an evaluator" |
| "zero scaffold rules remain" | "KSI-011…014 remain **scaffolds** (KSI-CMT) pending the CR26 VER evidence contract" |
| (silent on FRR) | "FRR: 9/17 Covered, 5 Partial, 3 External; **6 gap items are 2027-01-01 blockers**" |

---

## 5. The residual work (what actually closes open item #1)

Ordered by leverage:

1. **Reconcile the rule count (29 vs 14).** Confirm whether OrgComp's KSI-015…029 exist
   as rule files or are aspirational scaffolds; align the AR's asserted count to the
   files that exist. *This is the true blocker on "N/N satisfied."*
2. **Author the 15 zero-coverage indicators** (CED·INR·PIY·RPL·SCR). These themes
   were authored against the SCuBA/M365 surface, which never touched recovery,
   supply chain, incident response, or policy/inventory. Each needs a local rule
   bound to non-SCuBA telemetry.
3. **Finish the 10 partial-theme indicators** (CNA 6, MLA 3, SVC 4 — minus overlap).
4. **Make KSI-011…014 evaluable** — bind the KSI-CMT scaffolds to substrate change/
   drift telemetry (they exist but don't yet evaluate).
5. **Close the 6 FRR 2027-01-01 blockers** (G-CMU/IEC/IVV/SCN/SDR/VDR-01, UIAO_207 §6).
6. **Write the mapping back into the OrgComp spine** — populate the `ksi_ref` column of
   `aan-compliance-spine.yml` from UIAO_137, so the AR count is derived, not asserted.

---

## 6. Bottom line for the decision-gate

Open item #1 is not a reason to doubt UIAO — it is *evidence UIAO is already doing
the reconciliation work* (UIAO_137/UIAO_207 exist; OrgComp has no equivalent). It is a
reason to **stop asserting "29/29 satisfied" externally** until steps 1–2 land. The
honest current posture is: *46-indicator catalog known; 21 covered; 25 residual
enumerated; 6 FRR blockers dated.* That is a defensible ConMon baseline — a false
"100%" is not.
